extracted.intended_audience: NRSA (Ruth L. Kirschstein) fellowship reviewers and fellowship applicants / mentors
extracted.subtask_description: A PhD candidate's Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA Diversity Fellowship research proposal and training plan focused on immunology, containing Specific Aims, Significance, Innovation, Approach, preliminary data, timeline, and training activities. The rubric items reflect what reviewers will evaluate in such an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear, testable specific aims that state the primary objective(s) and hypotheses (e.g., Aim 1: Evaluate adipose tissue as a reservoir for replicative and persistent virus; Aim 2: Determine the response of adipose tissue CD8 T cells during mCMV infection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each aim should describe what will be tested, the working hypothesis, and link to overall objectives; include sub-aims and a graphical abstract/summary of aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why the problem is important and how the proposed work will advance understanding or clinical/biological importance (e.g., identifying adipose as an mCMV reservoir has implications for vaccine design and therapeutics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate clinical/biological importance, place proposal in context of existing literature, and justify why the question matters for the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe conceptual or technical novelty (e.g., first description of CMV infection and immunological consequences in adipose tissue; development of next-generation RNA Prime Flow probes for flow cytometry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state what is novel, how it shifts paradigms, and any technical innovations even if not the primary objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (Overall Research Strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed experimental approaches for testing hypotheses, including methods, timepoints, cohorts, and planned analyses (e.g., infections with Smith mCMV at 3x10^5 pfu, harvest at days 3, 7, 14; plaque assays and qPCR; flow cytometry phenotyping).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationale, stepwise plans, and integration of sub-aims; describe how data will be obtained and interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Present preliminary results that motivate the aims (e.g., ImmPort analysis showing correlation between adiposity and CMV index; Figure 3 showing increased mCMV-specific CD8 T cells in adipose at 7 dpi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use preliminary results to demonstrate feasibility and support hypotheses; tie prior observations to proposed experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental Design: Sample Size, Power, and Cohort Design
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify group sizes and cohort structure by power analysis (e.g., group sizes of 8 experimental and 8 control animals to detect >50% effect size at β=0.80 and α=0.05).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit power calculations, numbers per timepoint, and ensure design allows detection of biologically meaningful effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical Analysis & Significance Thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify statistical tests and significance criteria (e.g., Two-sample Student’s T test between tissues/products; one-way ANOVA for multi-group comparisons; p-value < 0.05 considered significant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State software (GraphPad Prism), which tests will be used for which comparisons, and how significance will be determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls and Comparators
rubrics_metrics.description: Include appropriate negative and positive controls and uninfected comparators (e.g., uninfected littermates, infected positive control tissues such as spleen or lungs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare infected vs uninfected tissues, include positive control tissues and procedural controls for assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple, Complementary Assays for Endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Use orthogonal methods to measure the same biological endpoint (e.g., plaque assay for infectious virus plus qPCR of viral DNA and reverse-transcribed cDNA for gene activation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine functional assays (plaque) with molecular assays (qPCR, transcript detection) to robustly detect replication/reactivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tissue Processing & Fractionation Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe methods to separate adipose components (e.g., centrifugation to separate buoyant adipocytes and pelleted SVF; culture SVF and buoyant fractions on MEFs to test for infectious virus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail processing steps, how fractions will be assayed separately, and how outcomes will inform which cell types harbor virus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Infected Cell Types
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to identify infected cells using reporter viruses and phenotyping (e.g., mCMV-eGFP-SL8 to detect eGFP+ infected cells; flow cytometry panels to discriminate macrophages, monocytes, neutrophils, T cells, NK cells, B cells, endothelial cells; include adipocyte markers if buoyant fraction infected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use validated markers, appropriate cytometers (BD Fortessa), and analysis software (FlowJo); include fallbacks (anti-eGFP antibody, RNA-Prime Flow probes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reactivation Assays and Multiple Reactivation Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Test for latent virus reactivation using several stimuli (pharmacological cyclophosphamide, total-body gamma irradiation 6 Gy with antibiotic follow-up, tissue culture explants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple reactivation approaches to increase chance of detecting reactivatable latent virus; include proper controls and timepoints for assay of reactivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated Results and Interpretation (including Null Outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: State expected outcomes and alternative interpretations (e.g., expect adipose viral load comparable to spleen early, later shifts to salivary gland; if no virus detected, consider trafficking/presentation of antigen to explain CD8 T cell presence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how each possible experimental outcome will be interpreted and what subsequent experiments will follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitfalls and Alternatives / Contingency Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit discussion of potential technical problems and alternate strategies (e.g., MEFs variability and switching to a protocol that allows greater viral spreading; use qPCR if plaques fail; use signal amplification or RNA-Prime Flow if eGFP flow detection insufficient).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate failures, state fallback assays, and explain how null results will still yield informative follow-up experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility: Independent Replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for independent replication of experiments (e.g., 'All experiments will be carried out, independently, at least twice').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that assays/experiments will be repeated independently to ensure reproducibility of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal Model Choice, Sex, Age, and Rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify use of specific animal strain, sex, and ages (e.g., male C57BL/6 mice 6–12 weeks to control for sex hormones and microbiota and to leverage available transgenic mice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide biological rationale for sex selection, strain choice, and how this impacts interpretation and generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal Care and Regulatory Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: State animal housing and procedural compliance (e.g., maintained in SPF animal facilities; procedures in accordance with The University of Arizona Animal Care and Use Committee requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document adherence to institutional animal care policies and biosafety procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization and qPCR Controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Use internal controls for molecular assays (e.g., GAPDH copy number as qPCR control when quantifying IE-1 and gB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify housekeeping genes and normalization strategy for quantitative molecular readouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Well-Characterized Reagents/Strains and Doses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use established viral strains and defined inocula (e.g., Smith strain of mCMV at 3x10^5 pfu by IP injection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite provenance of strains/methods and justify dose and route to align with prior literature and interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement per Tissue Mass
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify viral load normalized to tissue mass (e.g., tissues weighed and cut in half to quantify viral load per gram).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalize measurements to tissue weight to allow comparisons across tissues and timepoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Analysis Tools and Software
rubrics_metrics.description: State analytic tools to be used (e.g., GraphPad Prism for statistical analyses; FlowJo for cytometry data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify software and versions when relevant, and how data will be processed and visualized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Plan: Allocation of Effort and Career Development Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify trainee's planned activities and percent effort (e.g., Yearly breakdown Research: 80%, Seminars/Journal Club: 10%, Conferences/Career Development: 10%; attend and present at specified conferences; submit manuscripts and defend thesis in specified years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a year-by-year timeline with milestones (manuscripts, thesis defense, conferences) and percentage effort to demonstrate realistic training plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Goals, Mentorship, and Networking
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how mentorship and interactions with senior scientists will advance the trainee's career (e.g., supervision by Dr. Nikolich-Zugich, interactions with named leaders, involvement in program projects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how mentor network and collaborative environment will support technical training, independence, and future postdoctoral placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and Outreach / Recruitment of Underrepresented Trainees
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the applicant's involvement in diversity activities and commitment to increasing visibility of scientific careers to underrepresented students (e.g., student member of Department Diversity Committee; prior NIH IMSD funding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For diversity fellowships, describe past contributions, mentoring plans, and how funding will further outreach and development of underrepresented trainees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Competence & Feasibility Based on Prior Experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that the applicant and lab have the technical background required (e.g., experience with lateral flow assays, Magpix Luminex, CRISPR/Cas9, flow cytometry, peptide library biopanning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List specific techniques previously performed and how they support feasibility of the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development and Incorporation of New Methods/Technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Include development of novel detection technologies as part of the project (e.g., next-generation RNA-Prime Flow probes for viral transcripts for use in flow cytometry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how methodological innovation will be validated and how it complements primary aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit Timeline and Milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a multi-year timeline showing major milestones (e.g., Year 1: complete Aim 1; Year 2: submit manuscript on Aim 1 and complete Aim 2; Year 3: submit manuscript for Aim 2 and defend thesis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the timeline to demonstrate feasibility and training progression; tie milestones to grant duration.
